title: Missing Parenthesis
code:
def greet(name):
    message = 'Hello, ' + name
    print(message
    return message

bugs.explanation: print(message is missing its closing parenthesis. Python will raise a SyntaxError at runtime. It should be print(message).

title: The Classic Swap
code:
def swap(a, b):
    a = b
    b = a
    return a, b

bugs.explanation: Line 2 overwrites a with b's value before b is saved anywhere. By line 3, b = a just copies b back to itself. The fix is a, b = b, a (or use a temp variable).

title: Comparing to None

bugs.explanation: Use 'is None' instead of '== None'. The == operator can be overridden by a class's __eq__ method, giving wrong results. PEP 8 and Python idiom both require 'is None'.

title: Mutable Default Argument

bugs.explanation: The default value [] is created once when the function is defined, not on each call. Every call that omits 'collection' shares the same list, so items accumulate across calls. Use collection=None and set it inside the function instead.

title: Off by One Index

bugs.explanation: Valid indices run from 0 to len(items)-1. items[len(items)] is always one past the end and raises IndexError. Use items[len(items) - 1] or, more simply, items[-1].

title: Wrong Range Start

bugs.explanation: range(1, len(items)) starts at 1, so the element at index 0 is never included. Unless intentional, this should be range(len(items)) or range(0, len(items)).

title: Wrong else Return

bugs.explanation: When value is already within [lo, hi], the function should return value unchanged. Returning lo instead silently maps every in-range input to the lower bound.

title: Two Bugs: Bad Init + Typo

title: No Bug — Palindrome Check
Or vs And

bugs.explanation: Using 'or' allows anyone with a ticket (regardless of age) or anyone old enough (regardless of a ticket) to enter. If both conditions are required, the operator should be 'and'.

title: Off by One in Count

bugs.explanation: str.split() already returns exactly the words in the sentence. Subtracting 1 means a one-word input returns 0 and a two-word input returns 1, always undercounting by one.

Inside a regular Python string, \n is a newline and \t is a tab. The variable will contain 'C:' + newline + 'ew_folder' + tab + 'est.txt'. Use a raw string: r'C:\new_folder\test.txt', or escape the backslashes: 'C:\\new_folder\\test.txt'.

title: No Bug — Temperature Conversion
Wrong Letter Grade

bugs.explanation: Scores in the 70–79 range fall into this branch but it returns 'B' — the same as the 80–89 branch. It should return 'C'. The grade for 60–69 should be 'D', but that branch is unreachable until this one is fixed.

title: Off by One in Repeat

bugs.explanation: range(times + 1) produces times+1 iterations (0 through times inclusive), so the string is concatenated one extra time. It should be range(times) to repeat exactly 'times' times.
